newsitem.title: UK: Leicester City shareholders to vote on float plans.
newsitem.headline: Leicester City shareholders to vote on float plans.

text.p: English premier league soccer club Leicester City has confirmed plans for a stock market listing, calling a meeting of shareholders to approve changes paving the way for flotation.
The club's 120 shareholders have been asked to attend a meeting on May 9 to vote on changes to the company's structure required in advance of a listing.
The club said it hopes to join the market in June, although it has not yet decided whether to seek a full listing or to join the junior Alternative Investment Market (AIM).
Analysts believe League Cup finalists Leicester will seek to raise some 10-15 million stg in a flotation, which will value the club at 40-45 million stg.
There are now 15 British soccer clubs listed on the stock market, the sector being worth some 1.3 billion stg.
Former European champions Aston Villa and Bolton Wanderers, who have just won promotion to the premier league next season, will also join the market shortly.

The sector showed strong gains last year but prices have been under pressure in recent weeks. Shares in Newcastle United, which joined the market on April 2, stood at 126.5p on Tuesday, below their 135p issue price.
Leicester chairman Tom Smeaton said in a letter to shareholders that fresh funds were needed to strengthen the squad, finance youth development and improve the club's Filbert Street stadium.
"A flotation will allow us to raise money in the City (of London) and continue to compete at the highest level," he said.
